usage: Used as a countable noun for a natural spring; in Cantonese it usually refers to a water source coming out of the ground.
Common in geography, travel, and place descriptions. It sounds neutral and standard, not slangy.
Often appears in compound nouns or place names, especially when talking about water, mountains, or natural scenery.
Learners can use it to name a feature directly, without needing an extra classifier in most everyday descriptions.
